target: Eu costumo dormir cedo.
english: I usually go to sleep early.
tip: 'Costumar' + infinitive means 'to usually do something.' It's the most natural way to express habits in Portuguese.

target: Nós estudamos juntos na biblioteca.
english: We study together at the library.
tip: Regular -ar verbs: estudar → nós estudamos. The -amos ending is the same for all regular -ar verbs.

target: Ele estuda engenharia na universidade.
english: He studies engineering at the university.
tip: Regular -ar verbs: estudar → ele estuda. 'Numa' is the contraction of 'em + uma' (in a).

target: Eles jogam vôlei na praia.
english: They play volleyball at the beach.
tip: 'na' contracts em+a – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Eu procuro um emprego novo.
english: I'm looking for a new job.
tip: The present tense in Portuguese often translates as the present continuous in English: 'procuro' = I'm looking for.

target: Vocês pedem comida por delivery?
english: Do you order food for delivery?
tip: 'pedem' – irregular present tense. The most common Portuguese verbs are irregular and must be memorized individually.

target: Eles aprendem rápido quando praticam.
english: They learn fast when they practice.
tip: 'quando' – gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: Ela toca violão muito bem.
english: She plays the guitar very well.
tip: 'Violão' is the Brazilian word for acoustic guitar. 'Guitarra' in Brazil refers to an electric guitar.

target: Esse restaurante é caro demais.
english: This restaurant is way too expensive.
tip: 'Ser' describes inherent or permanent qualities – characteristics that define someone or something.

target: Você trabalha de segunda a sexta?
english: Do you work Monday through Friday?
tip: Yes/no questions in Portuguese often have the same word order as statements – intonation does the work.

target: Eu chego no trabalho às nove.
english: I get to work at nine.
tip: 'Chegar' uses the preposition 'em' for locations, not 'a' as in European Portuguese: 'chego no trabalho.'

target: Eu bebo água o dia inteiro.
english: I drink water all day long.
tip: Regular -er verbs: beber → eu bebo. The -er verbs use -o for 'eu,' just like -ar verbs.

target: Ela lê o jornal toda manhã.
english: She reads the newspaper every morning.
tip: Regular -er verbs: ler → ela lê. The circumflex accent on 'lê' marks the closed /e/ sound.

target: Eles trabalham numa empresa de tecnologia.
english: They work at a tech company.
tip: 'Trabalhar' is regular -ar. 'Numa' is the contraction of 'em + uma' – mandatory in Portuguese.

target: Você entende o que ele fala?
english: Do you understand what he says?
tip: 'Falar' (to speak/talk) is the model -ar verb in Portuguese. All regular -ar verbs follow its pattern.

target: Nós voltamos para casa às seis.
english: We go back home at six.
tip: 'Em casa' = at home (no article). 'Na casa dele' = at his house (article needed with possessive).

target: A gente acorda tarde no domingo.
english: We wake up late on Sundays.
tip: Think of a gente as "us folks". Singular verb form, plural meaning. A gente quer pizza = we want pizza.

target: Ele agenda as consultas pelo telefone.
english: He schedules the appointments by phone.
tip: 'pelo' contracts por+o – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: A gente paga tudo no cartão.
english: We pay for everything by card.
tip: 'A gente' (we, informal) takes the singular verb form: 'a gente fala' not 'a gente falamos.'

target: Nós gostamos de caminhar à noite.
english: We like to walk at night.
tip: Portuguese `gostar` always takes `de`: `gosto de pizza`, `gosto de você`. Drop the `de` and the sentence breaks. English `like` has no preposition; Portuguese needs one.

target: Eu posso te ajudar com isso.
english: I can help you with that.
tip: 'Poder' means can/to be able to. Its forms are irregular: posso, pode, podemos, podem. Use it for ability and permission.

target: Eu sei onde fica o restaurante.
english: I know where the restaurant is.
tip: 'Saber' means to know facts or how to do something. 'Sei' is the irregular eu form. 'Ficar' meaning 'to be located' is very Brazilian.

target: Eu vou fazer compras no shopping.
english: I'm going shopping at the mall.
tip: 'Ir + infinitive' forms the immediate future in Brazilian Portuguese. It's used much more often than the simple future tense in everyday speech.

target: Vocês podem vir para o jantar?
english: Can you come over for dinner?
tip: 'Vir' means to come and is irregular: venho, vem, vimos, vêm. Don't confuse 'vir' (to come) with 'ver' (to see).

target: Ele quer sair mais cedo hoje.
english: He wants to leave early today.
tip: `Tenho que + infinitive` = 'I have to': `tenho que sair` (I have to leave). Common alternative to `preciso/devo`.

target: A loja está fechada aos domingos.
english: The store is closed on Sundays.
tip: 'Estar' is used for states that can change – a shop being open/closed is a temporary condition.

target: O hotel é perto da praia.
english: The hotel is near the beach.
tip: 'Ser' is used for permanent location of buildings and landmarks – use 'estar' for people and movable things.

target: Minha mãe é uma ótima cozinheira.
english: My mom is a great cook.
tip: 'Ser' expresses identity, origin, and permanent characteristics – think of qualities that don't change day to day.

target: O que você está fazendo agora?
english: What are you doing right now?
tip: Endings: -ar → -ando, -er → -endo, -ir → -indo. `Comendo`, `bebendo`, `dormindo`. Always paired with `estar`.

target: Onde tem um bom restaurante japonês?
english: Where can I find a good Japanese restaurant?
tip: Brazilians use `tem` for 'there is/are' instead of `há`: `tem uma farmácia aqui` = 'there's a pharmacy here'. Same `ter` (to have) doing double duty.

target: Eu lavo a louça depois do jantar.
english: I wash the dishes after dinner.
tip: Regular -ar verbs: lavar → eu lavo. 'Louça' means dishes. 'Depois de' = after.

target: A gente leva marmita para o trabalho.
english: We bring packed lunches to work.
tip: 'Marmita' is a very Brazilian concept – a homemade meal in a container that you take to work or school. It's a huge part of daily life.

target: Ela joga tênis duas vezes por semana.
english: She plays tennis twice a week.
tip: 'Por' indicates cause, means, or exchange – contrast with 'para' which signals purpose or destination.

target: Ele participa de um grupo de corrida.
english: He participates in a running group.
tip: 'Participar de' means 'to participate in' or 'to be part of.' In Brazil, 'de' is used instead of 'em' after this verb.

target: Eu vou de ônibus para o trabalho.
english: I go to work by bus.
tip: 'Ir de' + transport: 'ir de ônibus' = go by bus. No article needed after 'de' for transport.

target: Ele é o mais velho dos irmãos.
english: He's the oldest of the siblings.
tip: Prepositions and articles fuse: de + o → do, de + a → da, em + o → no, em + a → na. Gender info still shows: na casa is feminine.

target: Eu sou casado e tenho dois filhos.
english: I'm married and have two children.
tip: Marital status uses 'ser' in Portuguese because it's seen as a defining characteristic, not a temporary state.

target: Uma hora de almoço não é suficiente.
english: One hour for lunch isn't enough.
tip: Portuguese nouns are masculine or feminine, even objects. o livro (m, the book), a casa (f, the house). Learn each noun with its article.

target: Eu tomo café da manhã às sete horas.
english: I have breakfast at seven o'clock.
tip: 'Tomar café da manhã' means 'to have breakfast.' 'Tomar' is used for drinking and for meals in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Eu ligo para a minha avó todo domingo.
english: I call my grandmother every Sunday.
tip: 'minha' – diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: Eu começo a trabalhar às oito em ponto.
english: I start working at eight sharp.
tip: 'Começar a' + infinitive means 'to start doing something.' The preposition 'a' is required after 'começar.'

target: Eu estou com fome, vamos comer alguma coisa?
english: I'm hungry, shall we eat something?
tip: 'Estar' expresses temporary states, conditions, and locations – things that could be different tomorrow.

target: Eu escuto música enquanto trabalho.
english: I listen to music while I work.
tip: 'Enquanto' means 'while' and connects two simultaneous actions in the present.

target: Vocês acham que vai chover?
english: Do you think it's going to rain?
tip: 'Achar que' is the casual Brazilian way to say 'to think that.' It's much more common than 'pensar que' in everyday speech.

target: Ela sabe cozinhar muito bem.
english: She knows how to cook very well.
tip: 'Saber' + infinitive = to know how to do something. 'Saber cozinhar' = to know how to cook.

target: Eu quero aprender a surfar.
english: I want to learn how to surf.
tip: Modal verbs attach directly to the infinitive: `preciso estudar`, `quero comer`. No preposition between. `Preciso de estudar` would be European Portuguese, not Brazilian.

target: Ela quer aprender a dirigir.
english: She wants to learn how to drive.
tip: `Tenho que + infinitive` = 'I have to': `tenho que sair` (I have to leave). Common alternative to `preciso/devo`.

target: A gente conversa muito no escritório.
english: We chat a lot at the office.
tip: 'A gente' means 'we' in casual Brazilian Portuguese and takes the ele/ela verb form, not the nós form.

target: Ele canta muito bem no chuveiro.
english: He sings really well in the shower.
tip: Regular -ar verbs: cantar → ele canta. Third-person singular drops -ar and adds -a.

target: Ela ensina matemática numa escola pública.
english: She teaches math at a public school.
tip: Regular -ar verbs: ensinar → ela ensina. 'Numa' = em + uma. These contractions are mandatory in speech.

target: Ela pratica yoga de manhã cedo.
english: She practices yoga early in the morning.
tip: 'De manhã' = in the morning. 'Manhã' also means 'tomorrow' – context tells you which.

target: Eu penduro a roupa no varal.
english: I hang the clothes on the clothesline.
tip: Adjectives match the noun. o carro vermelho (m sg), a casa vermelha (f sg), os carros vermelhos (m pl), as casas vermelhas (f pl).

target: Eu imprimo os documentos no escritório.
english: I print the documents at the office.
tip: 'Imprimir' has two past participle forms: 'imprimido' (regular) and 'impresso' (irregular). Both are correct in Brazil.

target: Vocês participam da reunião de quinta?
english: Will you be at Thursday's meeting?
tip: 'da' contracts de+a – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Ela pinta quadros no tempo livre.
english: She paints pictures in her free time.
tip: Prepositions and articles fuse: de + o → do, de + a → da, em + o → no, em + a → na. Gender info still shows: na casa is feminine.

target: Elas ensinam inglês numa escola particular.
english: They teach English at a private school.
tip: 'Num/numa' are contractions of 'em + um/uma.' They're standard in both speech and writing.

target: Vocês conversam em português no escritório?
english: Do you chat in Portuguese at the office?
tip: 'no' contracts em+o – mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Vocês fecham o escritório às seis?
english: Do you close the office at six?
tip: `Você` conjugates as 3rd singular (like `ele/ela`): `você é`, `você tem`, `você fala`. Don't try to use the `tu` forms unless you're learning European Portuguese.

target: Ela é médica num hospital público.
english: She's a doctor at a public hospital.
tip: 'Ser' for professions: 'Ela é médica.' No article is used between 'ser' and the profession in Portuguese.

target: Eu dou uma olhada nisso depois.
english: I'll take a look at that later.
tip: 'Dar uma olhada' means 'to take a look.' Brazilians love using 'dar + uma + noun' for quick actions: dar uma ligada (make a quick call), dar uma volta (take a walk).
